headline: All seven majors sit below their 200-day lines while momentum and flows tell a more mixed story underneath
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it settles the argument before anything else gets a vote. BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE and ADA are all below their 200-day moving averages, none showing a golden cross. That's a uniform, structurally bearish trend picture: seven for seven. BTC sits 48.6% off its 12-month high of $124,739.81, ETH is 60.4% off its high, and the smaller caps are worse, with ADA 80.9% off its peak. When every asset agrees on the trend direction, that's not noise, that's the tape's baseline.

Momentum is where it gets interesting, and where the divergence lives. RSI-14 readings are all mid-range (37.6 to 65.2), nobody stretched to an extreme. But MACD is split: SOL, BNB and DOGE are showing MACD above signal even while their price sits deep below the 200-day, meaning short-term momentum is perking up inside a longer downtrend. BTC and ETH show the opposite pairing, RSI comfortably above the midline (49.5 and 55.1) but MACD still below signal. That's a trend that hasn't confirmed a turn even as short-term price action (BTC +0.82% today, +9.38% over 30 days; ETH +1.53% today, +21.62% over 30 days) has been constructive. Worth naming plainly: momentum is trying to lead trend here, and trend hasn't followed yet.

Positioning adds a layer of fragility. BTC funding is running at 3.4% annualized, mild but positive, meaning longs are paying to hold the trade, with a long/short account ratio of 1.61. DOGE and XRP carry the most crowded long books (ratios of 4.17 and 3.35, funding annualized at 8.9% and 7.4%), which is expensive positioning stacked on one side. SOL is the odd one out: funding is negative (-3.9% annualized, shorts paying longs) even though the long/short ratio shows 2.04, more long accounts than short. Liquidations over the last day back up the wobble: BTC longs took $6.01M in liquidations against $1.36M for shorts, while ETH saw a much more balanced flush ($8.63M longs vs $8.52M shorts), and DOGE actually liquidated more shorts than longs ($456K vs $146K) despite its heavily long positioning. That's crowded books getting tested from both directions, not a one-way squeeze.

Flows are where the traditional-finance bid and the whale ledger disagree with each other. On August 11, BTC spot ETFs took in a net $7.8M, with the five-session total at +$346.9M, though same_direction_days of 1 means that string just turned and hasn't built a run yet. ETH ETFs printed -$1.7M on the same day but are net +$186.2M over five sessions (same_direction_days of 2). Meanwhile the whale ledger over the past 48 hours shows $46.9M moving onto exchanges on net, driven by BTC specifically ($103.1M onto exchanges), while ETH moved the other way ($56.2M off exchanges). The weekly whale series (-$243.8M, +$1.18B, +$1.12B, -$692.8M) has been swinging hard session to session, so today's negative reading sits inside a choppy pattern, not an established direction. Stablecoin float, the market's dry powder, is essentially flat to slightly down, off 0.98% over 30 days to $306.4B.

Sentiment sits at 27, labeled Fear, but that's actually mid-pack against its own 30-day range of 22 to 33, not a fresh extreme. So the crowd is uneasy without being panicked, while ETF desks added money on the latest print and whale wallets sent BTC toward exchanges. That's a genuine split between what the gauge says and what the money did on the same day, and it's worth sitting with rather than resolving.

What to watch from here: whether BTC and ETH can flip MACD above signal to match their already-positive RSI, whether the ETF same-direction-day counter builds past one or two sessions into an actual run, and whether the whale net flips back toward exchanges-outflow the way it did two weeks ago when the weekly series printed +$1.18B and +$1.12B in a row. Any one of those would change which side of this divergence is actually leading.
